ideas.title: Twin Ember
ideas.concept: Two palm-sized stones that connect a pair of people living alone. When one person holds theirs, the other slowly warms and glows like a shared fire, signaling presence without messages or notifications.
ideas.mechanism: Capacitive touch sensor detects holding; low-power radio (LoRa or BLE) sends a silent signal; the paired stone activates a resistive heater and warm LED over 30–60 seconds.
ideas.first_step: Build two Arduino-based prototypes with heating pads, warm LEDs, and LoRa modules, then test range and warmth timing in two homes.

ideas.title: City Window
ideas.concept: A tabletop device with a physical dial and speaker that plays live, low-fidelity ambient audio from rotating public places—a café, park, library, or market. It gives the felt sense of being near other people without interaction or feeds.
ideas.mechanism: Cellular/Wi-Fi stream from pre-approved public microphones; a physical knob selects a channel; an internal schedule rotates locations automatically. No screen, no app, no user input beyond turning it on.
ideas.first_step: Partner with a local public radio station or library to install one weatherproof microphone in a public space and stream its audio to a prototype receiver.

ideas.title: Warmling
ideas.concept: A plush, non-verbal companion that breathes, warms, and shifts gently when touched. It has no voice and no app. Over time it learns your presence and initiates a slow breathing rhythm to sync with yours, reducing the ache of an empty room.
ideas.mechanism: Pressure and motion sensors detect touch and stillness; a microcontroller drives a silent air pump or motor for breathing motion, a heating element for warmth, and simple adaptive timing.
ideas.first_step: Sew a plush prototype around an Arduino, small fan, and heating pad, then test whether users find the breathing and warmth calming over a week of daily use.

polished: Twin Ember: two palm-sized stones connect two people living alone. Holding one triggers capacitive sensing and low-power LoRa/BLE; the paired stone's resistive heater and warm LED activate over 30–60 seconds, warming and glowing like a shared fire to signal presence without messages/notifications. Build two Arduino prototypes with heating pads, LEDs, LoRa, then test range and warmth timing in two homes.

City Window is a tabletop dial-and-speaker device playing live, low-fidelity ambient audio from rotating public places: cafés, parks, libraries, markets. Pre-approved microphones stream over cellular/Wi-Fi; a knob selects channels; a schedule rotates locations. No screen, app, or input beyond power. First step: partner with a local public radio station or library to install weatherproof microphone and stream to prototype receiver.

Warmling is a plush, voiceless, appless companion. It breathes, warms, shifts gently when touched. Pressure/motion sensors detect touch and stillness; a microcontroller drives silent air pump or motor, heating element, adaptive timing. Learns presence, initiates slow breathing to sync with user, reducing empty-room ache. Sew prototype around Arduino, small fan, heating pad tests breathing/warmth calming over week of daily use.

ideas.title: Hearthstone Pair
ideas.concept: A pair of palm-sized, smooth ceramic stones that share a silent, ambient sense of presence between two people who live apart. One stone stays with you, the other with a loved one. When either person rests a hand on their stone, the other stone gently warms to body temperature and emits a slow amber pulse for a few minutes, then fades. There are no screens, messages, or notifications—just a wordless 'I'm here' that requires no daily app check-in.
ideas.mechanism: Each stone contains a rechargeable battery, a capacitive touch sensor, a low-power radio (LoRa or Wi-Fi via a small base station), a heating element, and a soft LED. Touching one stone sends a signal to its paired stone over the internet or direct long-range radio. The receiving stone warms and pulses. After a one-time setup, the stones operate automatically and passively. If neither stone is touched for 24 hours, the other softly glows once as a gentle invitation, still without needing an app.
ideas.first_step: Build a prototype with two ESP32 boards, capacitive touch sensors, heating pads, and a simple MQTT broker or cloud relay; then test with two households for one month to see whether the ambient warmth and pulse reduce feelings of isolation without becoming another screen to check.

ideas.title: Warmth Pair
ideas.concept: A pair of palm-sized, smooth stones that let two people share a silent, physical sense of presence. When one person holds their stone, the other stone gently warms up, no matter the distance. No screens, no sounds, no messages.
ideas.mechanism: Each stone contains a capacitive touch sensor, a low-power long-range radio (LoRa), a rechargeable battery, and a flexible heating element. Holding one stone triggers a signal to the paired stone, which slowly warms to skin temperature over five minutes. It works without any daily app interaction.
ideas.first_step: Build a prototype using two Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense boards, LoRa modules, and flexible heating pads, then encase them in smooth, 3D-printed river-stone shells.

ideas.title: Ember Stone
ideas.concept: A palm-sized, ceramic stone that sits on a shelf and emits a slow, warm glow plus a subtle vibration when other Ember Stones nearby are active, creating a wordless sense of neighborhood co-presence for people who live alone.
ideas.mechanism: Each stone contains a passive infrared motion sensor, a LoRa mesh radio, a warm LED, and a haptic motor. When it senses movement in its own home, it broadcasts an anonymous, non-identifying 'presence pulse.' Other stones within range translate received pulses into a gentle breathing light or soft thrum. It never conveys who is there, only that someone nearby is moving through their day. A one-time setup app adjusts sensitivity; no daily app use is required.
ideas.first_step: Prototype two units with Arduino, PIR sensors, LoRa shields, and LED/haptic drivers; test at 0.5-mile range and tune pulse patterns to feel calming and ambient rather than monitoring-like.

polished: Hearthstone Pair is two palm-sized ceramic stones for people living apart. Touching one signals its paired stone, which warms to body temperature and emits a slow amber pulse and fades. It uses touch sensors, radio, heater, LED, battery; no screens or messages. After setup, automatic; if untouched 24 hours, it glows once. Prototype uses ESP32s and MQTT for two-household testing.

Warmth Pair: palm-sized smooth stones for two people to share silent physical presence. Holding one signals the other, at any distance, to warm to skin temperature over five minutes. Each has capacitive touch, LoRa radio, rechargeable battery, and flexible heater. No app, screens, sounds, or messages. Prototype: Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense, LoRa modules, flexible heating pads, 3D-printed river-stone shells.

Ember Stone is a palm-sized ceramic shelf object for wordless co-presence among people living alone. PIR, LoRa mesh, warm LED, haptic motor. Movement sends anonymous presence pulse; nearby stones turn pulses into warm breathing light or soft vibration, never who, only that someone nearby moves. One-time app sets sensitivity; no daily app use. Prototype two Arduino/PIR/LoRa/LED-haptic units, test 0.5-mile range.

ideas.title: Aromafuge
ideas.concept: A countertop appliance that captures volatile aroma molecules lost during cooking, concentrates them, and re-infuses them into the finished dish just before serving. It restores fresh herb, spice, and Maillard aromas that normally escape into the kitchen air.
ideas.mechanism: A Peltier-cooled cold trap condenses steam and headspace volatiles onto a chilled surface; a replaceable zeolite/activated-carbon cartridge adsorbs aroma compounds. At plating, controlled heating desorbs the concentrate, and a piezo microjet deposits it as a fine mist onto the food.
ideas.first_step: Build a bench prototype with a Peltier cold trap and a small adsorbent cartridge, then use GC-MS to measure capture and release efficiency for garlic, onion, and coffee volatiles.

ideas.title: Sonic Texture Loom
ideas.concept: A countertop chamber that programs the internal texture of food without frying or cooking it through. It can make a potato crispy outside and creamy inside, or tenderize meat, by applying precise acoustic cavitation patterns.
ideas.mechanism: A 40 kHz phased ultrasonic array creates localized cavitation zones inside food under closed-loop temperature control. Acoustic holography steers energy to specific depths, disrupting cell walls selectively. A camera and puncture sensor map texture in real time.
ideas.first_step: Test potato cubes in a water-coupled ultrasonic tank: vary cavitation dose and temperature, then measure texture with puncture tests and confocal microscopy.

ideas.title: Allergen Eraser
ideas.concept: A countertop microfluidic reactor that reduces specific allergens in liquid foods such as broths, purees, sauces, and beverages while preserving flavor. It targets proteins like gluten, dairy, or egg white at the point of use.
ideas.mechanism: Food circulates through a replaceable cartridge packed with immobilized enzymes on food-safe beads. A peristaltic pump and inline pH/temperature sensors maintain optimal digestion conditions. A final UV/heat step deactivates the enzymes before dispensing.
ideas.first_step: Prototype a cartridge with papain or pepsin immobilized on chitosan beads, then test gliadin degradation in a broth using ELISA.

polished: Aromafuge: countertop appliance capturing cooking-lost volatile aroma molecules, concentrating and re-infusing them into finished dishes before serving, restoring fresh herb, spice, Maillard aromas otherwise lost to kitchen air. Peltier-cooled trap condenses steam/headspace volatiles; replaceable zeolite/activated-carbon cartridge adsorbs aroma compounds. Heating desorbs concentrate; piezo microjet mists food. First, bench prototype with Peltier trap and adsorbent cartridge; GC-MS tests garlic/onion/coffee release efficiency.

Sonic Texture Loom: countertop chamber programming internal texture without frying/cooking through. A 40 kHz phased ultrasonic array creates localized acoustic cavitation under closed-loop temperature control. Acoustic holography steers energy to depths, selectively disrupting cell walls. Camera and puncture sensors map texture. Crispy-outside/creamy-inside potato, tender meat. Tests vary cavitation dose/temperature on potato cubes in water-coupled tank, measuring puncture and confocal microscopy.

Countertop microfluidic reactor reduces allergens in liquid foods (broths, purees, sauces, beverages) preserving flavor. Targets gluten, dairy, egg-white proteins at point of use. Food passes through replaceable cartridge of immobilized enzymes on food-safe beads; peristaltic pump and inline pH/temperature sensors maintain optimal digestion; UV/heat deactivates enzymes before dispensing. Prototype: papain/pepsin on chitosan beads tests gliadin degradation in broth via ELISA.

ideas.title: ChronoRipe
ideas.concept: A countertop appliance that actively schedules the ripening of fruits and vegetables to peak on a chosen day, rather than just slowing spoilage like a refrigerator or speeding it up passively like a fruit bowl.
ideas.mechanism: Multiple sealed countertop compartments each contain an ethylene sensor, temperature/humidity sensor, Peltier cooler/heater, ultrasonic humidifier, photocatalytic ethylene scrubber, and a micro-dosing valve from a food-grade ethylene cartridge. A microcontroller reads each item's respiration and ethylene output, then adjusts temperature, humidity, and ethylene concentration—adding ethylene to accelerate ripening or scrubbing it to delay ripening—until the user-selected peak date.
ideas.first_step: Build a single-compartment prototype with an ethylene sensor, Peltier module, humidity control, and a potassium permanganate ethylene scrubber, then test whether it can hold bananas at a target ripeness stage for 24 hours.

ideas.title: Sonic Sphere Chef
ideas.concept: A countertop appliance that automatically creates filled edible spheres—like reverse-spherified ravioli, popping boba, or faux caviar—with precise size, skin thickness, and liquid filling, a task no current kitchen appliance performs.
ideas.mechanism: Peristaltic pumps dose a flavored liquid with calcium lactate and a separate alginate bath. A coaxial nozzle forms droplets that fall into the sodium alginate bath, where a camera and ultrasonic agitator monitor and control sphere formation. After a timed curing cycle, the spheres are rinsed and dispensed.
ideas.first_step: Build a two-channel peristaltic pump and coaxial needle prototype to test consistent droplet size and skin formation in a sodium alginate bath.

ideas.title: RipenPod
ideas.concept: A countertop produce ripening and preservation pod that actively controls ethylene, CO2, humidity, and temperature to ripen fruit to a chosen stage by a chosen time, or pause ripening to extend shelf life.
ideas.mechanism: A sealed chamber with ethylene, CO2, humidity, and temperature sensors. A microcontroller releases food-safe ethylene from an ethanol cartridge via a heated catalyst, scrubs CO2 with a zeolite filter, adjusts humidity and temperature, and uses UV-C to inhibit mold. The user selects a target ripeness date or a hold period.
ideas.first_step: Build a sealed 5-liter countertop chamber with temperature/humidity control and an ethylene sensor, then run controlled ethylene exposure trials on avocados to map ripening curves.

polished: ChronoRipe is a countertop appliance with sealed compartments. Each has ethylene/temp/humidity sensors, Peltier cooler/heater, humidifier, photocatalytic ethylene scrubber, and ethylene micro-dosing valve. Microcontroller adjusts temperature, humidity, and ethylene—adding to accelerate or scrubbing to delay—to ripen produce to chosen date, not just slow spoilage or passively speed ripening. Single-compartment prototype will test holding bananas at ripeness for 24 hours.

Sonic Sphere Chef: countertop appliance automatically creating filled edible spheres (reverse-spherified ravioli, popping boba, faux caviar) with precise size, skin thickness, and liquid filling, unlike appliances. Peristaltic pumps dose calcium-lactate liquid and alginate bath. Coaxial nozzle forms droplets into sodium alginate; camera and ultrasonic agitator monitor/control formation. Curing, rinse, dispense. Build two-channel peristaltic pump/coaxial needle prototype; test consistent droplet/skin formation.

RipenPod: countertop produce ripening/preservation pod controlling ethylene, CO2, humidity, temperature to ripen fruit; users choose target stage/time or hold period. Chamber sensors feed microcontroller releasing food-safe ethylene from ethanol cartridge/heated-catalyst, scrubbing CO2 with zeolite, adjusting humidity/temperature, and UV-C inhibiting mold. First: build sealed 5-liter chamber with temperature/humidity control and ethylene sensor; run controlled avocado ethylene trials to map ripening curves.

ideas.title: Grout Phantom Touch
ideas.concept: A grain-of-salt piezoelectric crystal embedded in floor grout that fires one randomly-timed pulse a day, making a lone person feel as if someone brushed past their ankle — manufactured company with no app, no network, no chatbot.
ideas.mechanism: A pinned ferroelectric domain wall in the crystal unpins and snaps, emitting a single acoustic emission (a 'click'). Coupled through the tile and floor into skin mechanoreceptors, one sub-threshold pulse reads as a light brush — a false touch. Because it fires at random intervals and you never know when, the ambiguity ('was that me or not-me?') is the actual product: the feeling of a presence rather than a device.
ideas.first_step: Pot a single piezo disc under one floor tile, drive it with one randomly-timed pulse per day, and ask a barefoot subject whether they report a phantom brush on the ankle.

ideas.title: The Moving Null
ideas.concept: A room tuned to an infrasound standing wave whose zero-motion node is a locatable 'hole in sound' that shifts as you move — a companion shaped like an absence you can find.
ideas.mechanism: Driving a room mode at infrasound frequency creates a standing wave with a pressure node: a point of near-zero motion and constant pressure, effectively a tiny absence. The node's position depends on your body's presence and movement, so the 'silence' moves with you. You learn where the null is and feel accompanied by a locatable hole rather than by any object — the room becomes an instrument played by your absence.
ideas.first_step: Drive a subwoofer at a measured room-mode frequency, map the pressure null with a microphone, and test whether a person can reliably locate the null and track it as they move.

polished: A grain-of-salt piezoelectric crystal in floor grout fires one random daily pulse, making a lone person feel an ankle brush. A pinned ferroelectric domain wall unpins and snaps, emitting an acoustic click; through tile/floor to skin mechanoreceptors, it reads as sub-threshold false touch. Random timing makes self/not-self ambiguity product. No app/network/chatbot. Testing: piezo disc under tile, daily pulse, barefoot subject.

The Moving Null drives a room at an infrasound standing-wave frequency, creating a near-zero-motion, constant-pressure node. It shifts with your body and movement, so you can locate and track absence and feel accompanied by a hole, not an object; the room becomes an instrument played by that absence. Test with subwoofer at measured room mode, microphone mapping, and reliably locating/tracking.

ideas.title: The String (a knot in the universe)
ideas.concept: A ceramic bead holding a single vibrating string at the Planck scale, entangled with every other String-bead in the world; touching your bead makes every other bead resonate. Not a message, not an app — a shared vibration, the smallest possible proof you are not alone.
ideas.mechanism: At 10^-35 m a string is indistinguishable from space itself, so entangling strings is really entangling the fabric of space; a touch excites your string and, through that shared substrate, every other string vibrates in sympathy. Why it works: it reframes loneliness as 'the silence between vibrations' and answers it with a guaranteed, wordless resonance — the universe itself as the medium, so no pairing, no network, and no daily opening is needed.
ideas.first_step: Prototype the felt experience at a feasible scale — a ceramic bead with a piezo that, when touched, broadcasts a single 'vibration' to all other beads, which hum in response — and test whether a message-free, global shared resonance reduces felt loneliness in a small pilot.

ideas.title: Quiet Mesh stone
ideas.concept: A palm-sized recycled-concrete stone with a soft warm LED core and a LoRa radio. Touching it sends a silent, anonymous pulse into a neighborhood mesh; other stones within ~1 km occasionally answer with a slow, breath-like glow. No screen, mic, camera, app, identity, or message — just a physical reminder that you are not the only one alone.
ideas.mechanism: A flooding protocol with random 1–60 minute delays: a node that receives a pulse does not forward it, it just contributes its own glow, so presence is felt but never traced or compared. Because there is nothing to see but light and no exposed IDs, the mesh cannot curdle into a feed, a graph, or a performance — it sidesteps the network/chatbot/notification failure modes by design.
ideas.first_step: Build two prototype stones (ESP32 + 900 MHz LoRa, one capacitive pad, one warm LED) and confirm that a touch on stone A produces a delayed, random glow on stone B.

ideas.title: Presence Stone (the building hums back)
ideas.concept: A palm-sized river stone with a solar cell and piezo that sits on the windowsill, listens to your home, and hums a low note when the house gets too quiet; other stones in the building hum along through the power lines. No app, no chat — just a hum that says the building is not empty.
ideas.mechanism: A piezo/mic senses ambient sound level; when the home stays below a quietness threshold, the stone drives a piezo to emit a low hum. It also couples a faint tone onto the mains wiring (power-line communication), so every other stone in the building receives it and hums in sympathy — turning the building's existing electrical grid into a shared, passive presence channel. Why it works: it converts the absence of human sound into a positive, ambient signal of co-presence, satisfying the stated requirement of 'physical, passive, no daily app,' and it scales from one home to a whole building with no pairing or setup.
ideas.first_step: Build one stone with a solar cell, a piezo disc, and a quietness detector, and test whether a low hum triggered by prolonged silence reads as presence rather than noise; then add two more and try coupling a simple tone over the power line to see if they hum together.

polished: A ceramic bead holds a Planck-scale string entangled with every other bead; touching one makes all resonate through space itself. It is not a message or app but wordless shared vibration, reframing loneliness as silence between vibrations. A piezo prototype broadcasts touches to humming beads, testing in a pilot whether resonance with no pairing, network, or daily opening reduces loneliness.

A palm-sized recycled-concrete stone holds a warm LED core and LoRa radio. Touch sends a silent anonymous pulse to stones within ~1 km, which occasionally answer with slow glow after random 1–60-minute delays. Nodes do not forward pulses; they glow. No screen, mic, camera, app, identity, or message. This avoids feeds, graphs, notifications. ESP32 LoRa prototypes will test delayed glow.

A palm-sized river stone with solar cell and piezo sits on windowsill. A piezo/mic senses ambient sound; below quietness threshold, it emits low hum. It couples faint tone onto mains wiring, so other building stones hum along, turning electrical grid into shared passive presence channel without apps, pairing, or setup. Test one hum for presence, then two with power-line coupling.

ideas.title: Sonic Molecular Controller ("Gastronome")
ideas.concept: A microwave-sized countertop chamber that runs closed-loop, state-based control of food biochemistry: the user picks a target molecular state ("ripen to peak flavor", "temper dark chocolate", "marinate chicken", "pasteurize eggs") and the device actuates with pulsed ultrasound/heat/pressure/humidity while reading the food's actual chemical composition every few seconds, stopping at the exact molecular moment rather than on a timer.
ideas.mechanism: A NIR spectrometer chip (e.g. TI NIRscan Nano, ~$200-500) with a broad-spectrum source and detector mounted above the food measures moisture, fat, protein, sugar and specific compounds (capsaicin, caffeine, etc.) in real time; an array of cheap piezo ultrasonic transducers on the bottom/sides provides non-thermal actuation — cavitation, mixing, emulsification, accelerated enzymatic reactions — and also stirs the food to defeat NIR's few-mm penetration limit. An ML model maps spectra to composition, compares against the target profile, and adjusts actuation in a loop. This closes the loop every current appliance leaves open (they follow preset time/temp and sense only proxies like temperature), enabling it to stop a ripening process at peak flavor, reverse a phase separation, re-crystallize chocolate to the right polymorph, or pasteurize without cooking by monitoring protein denaturation.
ideas.first_step: Buy a handheld NIR spectrometer plus one cheap ultrasonic transducer and driver; place a single sample (a ripening banana or a bar of chocolate) in a small sealed chamber and log NIR spectra over time while sonicating, to confirm you can detect a measurable spectral shift that tracks the ripening/tempering state.

ideas.title: The Demixer — a countertop appliance that un-mixes food
ideas.concept: A countertop appliance that runs blending in reverse: feed it a homogeneous mixture (a smoothie, a pureed soup, a vinaigrette) and it separates the mixture back into its constituent ingredients — strawberry puree, banana puree, yogurt, ice, air — each routed to its own output. No current appliance does this; every kitchen machine today only combines or homogenizes.
ideas.mechanism: Each ingredient carries a distinct physical signature — density, particle size, surface charge, and chirality — so a staged separation cascade can peel components off one axis at a time. A centrifuge first splits by density (ice and air float, purees sink), a microfluidic size sorter then separates particles by diameter, and a graphene-oxide membrane stack filters by charge and molecular size, with acoustic tweezers available to nudge the finest fractions. Because the signatures are orthogonal, stacking the stages lets a single countertop unit resolve a many-ingredient blend into separate streams rather than just two layers.
ideas.first_step: Prove one axis on a two-component mixture: spin a strawberry-banana smoothie in a benchtop centrifuge (or a salad vinaigrette) and confirm you can cleanly recover distinct density layers, then add a single microfluidic sorter to split one of those layers by particle size.

polished: A microwave-sized countertop chamber controls food biochemistry in closed loop. The user selects a target molecular state; NIR spectroscopy measures composition every few seconds, an ML model compares it to the target, and piezo ultrasound, heat, pressure, and humidity actuate until reached. Unlike preset time/temperature appliances, it stops at the molecular moment. Initial test: sonicate banana/chocolate, log NIR spectra.

The Demixer is a countertop appliance that reverses blending, separating a homogeneous food mixture into constituent ingredient streams, including air, via staged cascades. It exploits orthogonal signatures—density, particle size, surface charge, chirality—using centrifugation, microfluidic sorting, graphene-oxide membranes, and acoustic tweezers. Existing kitchen machines only combine or homogenize. Initial work: recover density layers from a two-component mixture, then size-split one layer.

ideas.title: The Un-Mixer: a countertop appliance that edits the oil–water interface
ideas.concept: A 20 cm cube next to the toaster that takes a jar of mayonnaise and gives back oil, yolk, and vinegar in three wells — not by spinning it, but by pulling the emulsion apart droplet by droplet and, more importantly, by rewriting the surfactant skin between the phases. It is an interfacial printer, not a separator: it can thicken, thin, fold, or pattern the interface, and even write a word into the surfactant layer.
ideas.mechanism: A glass tray feeds a microfluidic channel where a grid of microelectrodes applies dielectrophoretic/electrocoalescence fields to drive oil droplets out of the emulsion and hold them in a separate channel, while Peltier elements set the temperature that tunes surfactant solubility and phase behavior. Because the appliance controls the interface rather than just the bulk phases, the same hardware can be run in reverse as a printer: locally dosing surfactant, ions, or charge at the oil–water boundary changes how the droplet tastes and flows. Pushing the resolution down, a nanopore plus an on-chip optical trap catches a single lecithin molecule and rotates it so a chosen end faces the water — one molecule's orientation shifting the taste of the whole droplet.
ideas.first_step: Dilute a spoonful of mayonnaise into water, push it through a Y-channel with a single pair of electrodes, and confirm under a phone camera that oil droplets migrate to one outlet and leave a clearer aqueous stream at the other — the smallest possible proof that electrocoalescence separates an emulsion on a benchtop.

ideas.title: A box that makes a small darkness in the shape of a flavor
ideas.concept: The endpoint of the scale ladder: an appliance that absorbs one photon before it reaches the oil–water interface, so the interface is illuminated by a darkness with a shape — and that shape is a missing taste. The device is a countertop box that produces a shadow in the form of a flavor rather than a flavor itself.
ideas.mechanism: If the interface is a photoswitchable surfactant monolayer, then light arriving at it changes surface tension, charge, and packing, and therefore taste. Blocking a single photon at a chosen point means the interface there never receives its cue, leaving a patterned deficit — a dark region whose geometry encodes a flavor. The appliance works by subtraction: it computes the light field that would produce a target interfacial pattern, then projects the complement, so the interface is written by what is withheld. The result is a taste defined by an absence, held as a shaped shadow on a surfactant layer.
ideas.first_step: Project a simple dark stripe (via a printed mask or an SLM) onto a photoswitchable surfactant monolayer spread on water in a petri dish, and measure with a Wilhelmy plate whether surface tension differs inside the shadow versus outside — the cheapest demonstration that a darkness can be written into an interface.

polished: The Un-Mixer is a countertop appliance editing the oil–water interface. It separates mayonnaise into oil, yolk, and vinegar in wells using microelectrodes in a microfluidic channel, with dielectrophoretic electrocoalescence fields and Peltier control. Reversed, it prints surfactant, ions, or charge, altering droplet taste and flow. Nanopore/optical trapping orients lecithin molecules. Test: dilute mayonnaise through an electrode Y-channel; camera confirms separation.

A countertop box makes a shaped darkness representing a flavor, not a flavor. It computes light field for a target pattern on a photoswitchable surfactant monolayer, then projects the complement, blocking one photon at points so surface tension, charge, packing, and taste change by absence. A first test projects a dark stripe and measures surface tension with a Wilhelmy plate.

ideas.title: The Common Room Radio
ideas.concept: A small wooden radio that plays live, unedited ambient sound from a public third place—like a diner, library, or barbershop—so you feel quietly near other people without conversation or interaction.
ideas.mechanism: A cellular-enabled speaker with a single on/off/volume knob. It connects to a private audio stream from a discreet microphone in a partnered public space. No microphone on your end, no profiles, no messages, and no app required. It plays only during the venue's open hours, creating a low-fidelity sense of shared presence.
ideas.first_step: Partner with one local 24-hour diner to install a discreet microphone and stream ambient audio; prototype with a Wi-Fi speaker and a simple audio endpoint.

ideas.title: The Anthropotrope
ideas.concept: A living houseplant on a silent, self-contained turntable that turns to face you when you enter the room, and otherwise follows the light. It is a non-human roommate that notices you, requiring only weekly watering and no app. It provides a daily moment of being acknowledged, making a solitary home feel inhabited.
ideas.mechanism: A passive infrared sensor detects human presence and a light sensor detects ambient light. A microcontroller prioritizes the human signal, driving a stepper motor to rotate the plant's pot toward the person. When alone, it slowly turns to maximize light. The pot includes a water reservoir and holds a hardy plant like a snake plant. Power via USB or a small solar panel.
ideas.first_step: Build a prototype with a pothos plant, an Arduino, a PIR sensor, and a stepper motor. Program it to turn toward a person when detected. Then run a 2-week pilot with 10 people living alone, measuring subjective loneliness before and after, and conducting interviews about their relationship with the plant.

ideas.title: The Forager
ideas.concept: A living, non-human roommate in a sealed glass terrarium. It is a slime mold (Physarum polycephalum) that slowly explores a maze, learns to avoid obstacles, and forms intricate vein networks. You care for it by placing oats and adjusting humidity. It provides a sense of co-presence and a gentle daily routine without screens, apps, or simulated life. It fixes the criticism by being genuinely alive rather than a complex mechanical puppet, so it is not a novelty if you form a relationship. It is surprising because it is a slime mold, not a robot or a pet.
ideas.mechanism: A palm-sized glass or acrylic terrarium with a humid chamber, agar or moist paper substrate, and a removable maze insert. A magnifying lens and mirror let you observe its slow movements. A simple humidity indicator tells you when to mist. Food (oats) is placed in the maze to encourage exploration. The slime mold's movement is powered by its own biology; no electronics or app needed. You can train it to associate a gentle tap or a small flashlight pattern with feeding, so it anticipates your care.
ideas.first_step: Culture Physarum polycephalum in a petri dish and test whether a daily 1-minute observation and feeding routine reduces subjective loneliness in a 2-week pilot with 10 people living alone.

polished: Common Room Radio: small wooden cellular speaker with one on/off/volume knob. It plays private live, unedited ambient stream from a discreet mic in a partnered public venue—diner, library, barbershop—only during open hours. Low-fidelity shared presence without conversation, interaction, mic, profiles, messages, or app. Partner with 24-hour diner, install mic, stream audio; prototype with a Wi-Fi speaker and endpoint.

Anthropotrope: houseplant on a silent, self-contained turntable. Non-human roommate notices you, rotating pot toward entering person; otherwise follows light. PIR and light sensors feed a microcontroller; it prioritizes people, driving stepper motor. Alone, it maximizes light. Pot has water reservoir, plant, USB/solar, weekly watering, no app. Prototype: pothos, Arduino, PIR, stepper. Pilot: 10 solitary people, two weeks, loneliness measures, interviews.

The Forager. A living, non-human roommate in a sealed glass terrarium. It is a slime mold (Physarum polycephalum) that slowly explores a maze, learns to avoid obstacles, and forms intricate vein networks. You care for it by placing oats and adjusting humidity. It provides a sense of co-presence and a gentle daily routine without screens, apps, or simulated life. It
